correctness.rationale: The stationary conditional variance obeys a two-speed piecewise deterministic Markov evolution and has directly normalized gamma stationary densities. The entrance Palm distribution, exponential backward off-age, and common-rate gamma addition prove exact independence of the off-age fraction from both total variance and observed position. The posterior excess variance has explicit strictly convex rate Av+1/(2v), unique minimizer 1/sqrt(2A), and exponentially controlled tails; Slutsky yields the Beta age law. The on/off joint densities satisfy the exact posterior identity P(on|y)=1/(1+M_R), and the same saddle yields its sharp inverse-distance constant. A reproducible numerical checker independently compares finite-radius integrals but is not presented as proof of asymptotic limits.

Their explicit collective extreme-value scaling at strictly positive lower stiffness uses a bounded effective variance; the present strictly zero lower stiffness produces an unbounded conditional variance and conditions on a fixed-dimensional large observed displacement.

value.rationale: The exact law identifies how the current untrapped interval and inherited fluctuation variance jointly cause rare large displacements, a path-history question not answered by static spatial densities. A unique total-variance saddle coexists with a nonconcentrating Beta age fraction; this distinguishes microscopic excursion histories and supplies a parameter-resolved observable independent of spatial dimension. The sharp inverse-distance trap-state posterior complements this interpretation. The result is a motivated conditional classification, not an arbitrary gamma moment or textbook parameter substitution.
